[TASK_TYPE=explore]
[BOUNDARY=crypto+proof]
[SEVERITY=major]
If a batch certificate is still valid under the proof system but no longer bound to the exact batch public-input set, what kind of guarantee has privAI weakened?
It has weakened batch-binding integrity. The proof may still exist, but it is no longer tied to the exact public-input collection that the execution bundle is supposed to authorize.

[TASK_TYPE=explore]
[BOUNDARY=crypto+ledger]
[SEVERITY=critical]
What breaks first if signer-role checks are removed but signature verification remains?
Authorization semantics break first. The system can still detect that a key signed the message, but it can no longer prove that the signer was one of the policy-authorized roles for that action.

[TASK_TYPE=design]
[BOUNDARY=crypto]
[SEVERITY=major]
For long-term agility, should privAI bind its security model to one signature primitive or to protocol invariants above the primitive layer?

Bind the security model to protocol invariants above the primitive layer. Primitive choices can change, but signer-role binding, transaction-digest binding, replay protection, and layer separation should remain stable.
